proposal.summary: The Tutor LMS WordPress plugin (<= 1.5.2) is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) allowing an attacker to cause an admin to approve or block instructors via crafted GET requests and to add instructor accounts via CSRFed POST requests, potentially enabling the attacker to become an approved instructor.
proposal.affected_product: Tutor LMS WordPress plugin, version 1.5.2 and below
proposal.cwe_quote:
As the requests for the approval and blocking of instructors are sent using the GET method, the CSRF attack to approve an attacker-controlled instructor account can be performed by having the admin visit https://TARGET/wp-admin/admin.php?page=tutor-instructors&action=approve&instructor=8 directly,
after retrieving the instructor ID during the registration process.

AV.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

PR.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the plugin version in use and reproduce the described CSRF actions (GET approve/blocked endpoints and POST add instructor) against a test site. If confirmed, apply the vendor patch (Tutor LMS >= 1.5.3) or implement CSRF nonce checks and require POST+nonce for state-changing actions.
